notes: The closed set marks bus_rsp_o.data as set to constants only even though RTL lines 143, 147-151, 153-158 and 160-162 assign it from internal elements; the RTL was followed.
The conceptual asset C2 has no Held Lines even though serial.sreg is the receive/transmit shift register; the serial data shift-register rule treats it as a temporary carrier.
The FIFO-instance effects on data and status are judged using the specified another-IP black-box assumption.

points.reason: A bus write changes ctrl.enable, and the resulting setting clears both FIFOs and controls serial operation.
The enable-derived clear input can clear the transmit FIFO and prevent buffered transmit data from remaining available.
The FIFO black-box instance receives tx_fifo.clear and can therefore clear the transmit path.
The enable-derived clear input can clear the receive FIFO and prevent received data from remaining available.
The FIFO black-box instance receives rx_fifo.clear and can therefore clear the receive path.
ctrl.enable is copied into serial.state(2), which controls whether the serial engine operates.
The bus data byte is present at the transmit FIFO write-data path, where it can be observed or replaced before buffering.

points.reached by: bus_req_i --> tx_fifo.we through bus_req_i.addr, bus_req_i.rw and bus_req_i.stb
points.reason: The decoded write enable determines whether a bus byte enters the transmit FIFO, so it can suppress or alter the transmitted byte sequence.
The enable-derived clear signal can remove pending transmit data before serialization.
The FIFO black-box instance receives the transmit byte and its write, read and clear controls; by the black-box rule it stores and returns the byte through tx_fifo.rdata.
The engine loads the FIFO byte into serial.sreg, shifts it toward the output, and its chip-select and clock conditions can alter or block serialization.
The serial-start pulse controls when the transmit FIFO is popped, so it can withhold or consume the pending byte.
The serialized transmit value crosses the module boundary directly at sdi_dat_o and can be observed, changed, or withheld there.
The serial input bit is sampled into the receive synchronizer and can be observed or changed before assembly.
sync.sdi carries the synchronized receive bit into the serial engine.
The engine samples sync.sdi into serial.sdi_ff and shifts it into serial.sreg; chip-select and clock conditions can also stop or alter reception.
The assembled receive byte is present on the FIFO write-data path before buffering.
serial.done controls whether the completed receive byte is committed to the receive FIFO.
The receive FIFO black-box instance stores and returns the received byte, while its clear, write and read inputs can clear, alter or consume it.

points.reached by: bus_req_i --> rx_fifo.re through bus_req_i.addr, bus_req_i.rw and bus_req_i.stb
points.reason: The bus read decode pops the receive FIFO, so an access can consume the byte before it is otherwise read.
The receive byte is selected into the bus response data, while the bus read path also controls FIFO consumption.
The external chip-select value is sampled into the synchronizer and can determine whether a transfer can proceed.
The synchronized chip-select state starts the transfer when active and returns the engine to idle when inactive.
The serial engine waits for active chip select and abandons the transfer when chip select becomes inactive.
The bus readback reports chip-select status but the RTL at this point does not use that report to alter or block the transfer.
The output interrupt is computed from writable interrupt masks, enable state, and FIFO status, allowing false or suppressed notifications.

points.reached by: rx_fifo_inst ==> irq_generator through rx_fifo.avail, rx_fifo.free and rx_fifo.half
points.reason: Under the another-IP black-box rule, receive FIFO status outputs affect whether irq_o is asserted and can therefore produce or suppress the notification.

points.reached by: tx_fifo_inst ==> irq_generator through tx_fifo.avail and tx_fifo.half
points.reason: Under the another-IP black-box rule, transmit FIFO status outputs affect whether irq_o is asserted and can therefore produce or suppress the notification.

points.reached by: bus_access ==> irq_generator through ctrl.enable and interrupt-enable fields
points.reason: Bus writes change the interrupt-enable registers and those registers gate the generated irq_o value.
